audit_findings.title: Simmonds is inside the valuation-date perimeter but outside the OE series
audit_findings.magnitude: $757 million purchase price, equal to 2.30% of $32.933 billion base equity value or $12.77 per diluted share; omitted OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Simmonds earnings are absent from anchor OE while the June 2026 cash balance reflects the acquisition payment
audit_findings.evidence: On October 6, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of all the outstanding stock of the Simmonds Precision Products, Inc. Business (“Simmonds”) of Goodrich Corporation from RTX Corporation for approximately $757 million in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the filing does not isolate Simmonds' post-reinvestment OE. Purchase price provides scale but is not a measure of the omitted earnings' present value, so materiality cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Calculate Simmonds' pro forma after-tax OE, including maintenance capex and working capital, and rerun the anchor and bridge on one consistent June 2026 perimeter.

audit_findings.title: The OE anchor does not contain the current debt interest run-rate
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest-quarter interest expense-net was $514 million, annualizing to $2.056 billion, $484 million above FY2025's $1.572 billion and equal to 28.1% of the $1.722 billion OE anchor before tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring interest expense must reduce equity-level OE because debt principal is not deducted in the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: On August 19, 2025, the Company completed $5,000 million in new debt issuances.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing error: the historical anchor contains only partial interest on the August 2025 issuance and none of the later fiscal-2026 debt, while the forecast grows that stale anchor. The computed run-rate difference is large relative to anchor OE and is reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct annualized interest from every June 27, 2026 debt tranche, applicable SOFR, margins, swaps, collars, fees and interest income; apply the tax effect and rerun all scenarios from OE after the complete burden.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-dependent growth may be modeled without acquisition reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: At 61.9% RONTA, 7% growth requires 11.31% reinvestment, or $194.8 million on the $1.722 billion anchor; 10% growth requires 16.16%, or $278.2 million initially
audit_findings.mechanism: Required acquisition or organic reinvestment reduces forecast OE available to owners and compounds through forecast growth and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: A significant portion of our growth has occurred through acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the model already deducts reinvestment is unresolved, but the supplied growth rates and RONTA establish that a missing charge would be material. Compounding full OE while attributing growth to acquisitions would treat purchased growth as free, with particular impact because terminal value is 52.1% to 53.7% of base and bull operating value.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every forecast-year cash-flow formula for an explicit g divided by RONTA reinvestment deduction; if absent, rerun base and bull with that charge or replace acquisition-supported growth with documented organic post-reinvestment growth.

audit_findings.title: Declared dividend-equivalent liabilities may be an unbridged claim ahead of common stock
audit_findings.magnitude: $135 million accrued at September 30, 2025, of which $59 million was paid in fiscal 2026 YTD; the full opening balance equals 0.41% of base equity value or $2.28 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid dividend-equivalent liability is a claim deducted in the equity bridge unless already reflected in cash or OE
audit_findings.evidence: At September 30, 2025, there was $ 59 million recorded in accrued and other current liabilities and $ 76 million recorded in other non-current liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets related to future dividend equivalent payments.
audit_findings.explanation: Capture of the remaining liability is unresolved, but even omitting the entire filed $135 million opening balance would alter base value by only $2.28 per share, versus a $603.07 gap between the $555.65 base value and $1,158.72 market price. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on the demonstrated scale.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 27, 2026 current and non-current dividend-equivalent balances, reconcile the $59 million payment and subsequent accruals, and deduct only the unpaid amount not already reflected in cash or OE.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease capital consumption may escape both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 finance-lease amortization was $15 million, principal payments were $7 million and noncash finance-lease asset additions were $25 million; the June 2026 obligation was $313 million, 0.95% of base equity value or $5.28 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back finance-lease amortization without deducting replacement asset use or principal can overstate OE
audit_findings.evidence: The present value of the minimum finance lease payments, net of the current portion, represents a balance of $ 284 million and $ 262 million at September 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting pathway is demonstrated, but an actual omission from the OE workpaper remains unresolved. Filed annual amounts are small: $15 million of amortization is 0.87% and $25 million of additions is 1.45% of anchor OE; even the entire latest obligation is less than 1% of base equity value. This scale is insufficient to change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace finance-lease amortization, principal payments and noncash right-of-use additions through the OE workpaper; add a recurring asset-consumption deduction if absent and verify that no lease amount is double counted in debt or capex.
